title: FX Brief — 25 Nov 2026
intro: Asian trading is heavily pressured by a sharp regional tech sell-off as SoftBank drops 15 percent and AI spending concerns ripple through equities, while geopolitical risk rises following a Houthi attack on a Saudi infrastructure asset. The Swiss franc and Canadian dollar lead currency strength rankings, whereas the Australian dollar plummets following domestic inflation prints.

sections.heading: FX theme
sections.content: Risk sentiment dominates today as sliding global equities and lower crude oil weigh on pro-cyclical currencies, while upcoming US macro data including GDP and Core PCE keep major FX pairs reactive. Safe-haven demand provides strong bids for the Swiss franc and defensive positioning ahead of the US session.

sections.heading: Dollar read
sections.content: The US dollar index trades up 0.18 percent at 103.99 alongside subdued US 10-year yields down 1.4 basis points at 4.904 percent. The greenback benefits from safe-haven flows against lagging commodity currencies like the Australian dollar, while CHF and CAD outperform.

sections.heading: Crosses
sections.content: Yen and euro crosses reflect clear risk aversion with AUD/JPY down 0.88 percent and EUR/CHF falling 0.44 percent, highlighting broad liquidation in high-beta assets and flight to defensive currencies. Meanwhile, EUR/AUD surges 1.19 percent as the Australian currency bears the brunt of regional selling pressure.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▼ Bearish · AUD/USD — below 0.6550 opens 0.6420 · invalid above 0.6610*
Softer domestic inflation data and heavy regional tech-driven risk aversion weigh heavily on the Australian dollar.
- *▲ Bullish · USD/CHF — above 0.8400 opens 0.8550 · invalid below 0.8300*
Safe-haven inflows drive aggressive franc buying as broader equity indices and regional tech names retreat.
- *▲ Bullish · EUR/AUD — above 1.6700 opens 1.7100 · invalid below 1.6500*
- *▼ Bearish · S&P 500 — below 7,180.00 opens 7,000.00 · invalid above 7,250.00*
Growing debt and spending worries surrounding artificial intelligence spark a wider equity market correction.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions following infrastructure attacks
- Further contagion from the Asian tech and SoftBank equity sell-off into European and US sessions
